CLOSED-B at S231 across all four amortisation axes (a-direction trivial 8×; χ-direction 1.79-2.04× bounded constant; composite-q 1.75× bounded constant; Q-batched 1.05× decreasing toward 1×). None structural in algorithmic-complexity sense; all hardware-level FFT/BLAS arithmetic. No batch-polylog primes-in-AP algorithm via explicit-formula route. Thread-5-vs-Thread-6 distinction: Thread 5 partial-positive operates on SHARED-L geometry (ζ-zeros across queries); Thread 6 fails on DISTINCT-L geometry (distinct L(s, χ_q) per query). Future P_x targets should prioritise shared-L shapes.
thread_7_summary:Thread 7 = OPEN_POSITIVE_TARGETS.md §P3 — approximate pi(x) ± ε in polylog with named ε. R(x) gives ε ≈ √x. Question: can polylog buy ε = O(x^{1/2-δ}) for some explicit δ? With K=log²x zeros heuristically yields ε ≈ √x · O(log log x / log⁴ x) — strictly better-than-√x bound, polylog time. Smallest cross-domain barrier; pure analytic NT. Strongest a-priori chance of partial-positive based on R(x) error analysis from S195+S196 Galway frontier closure.
thread_7_a_grade_targets:(a) explicit polylog-time algorithm with provable ε(x) = O(x^{1/2}/polylog(x)) with named exponent → first sub-√x polylog approximation; (b) tight ε vs K characterisation across x decades (empirical Montgomery-validation); (c) lower bound matching ε ≥ Ω(√x/polylog(x)) under GRH or random-phase heuristic.
thread_7_slot_plan:
  slot_1: Build partial-sum evaluator π(x) ≈ R(x) - Σ_{ρ: |γ| ≤ T} 2 Re(li(x^ρ)) for K = {1, log x, log² x, log³ x, x^{1/4}, x^{1/2}} zeros. Empirical ε(x, K) at x ∈ {10⁶, 10⁸, 10¹⁰, 10¹²}. Fit ε vs K; identify saturation behaviour.
  slot_2: Theoretical extrapolation via Montgomery pair-correlation random-phase heuristic (S195 framework). Closed-form ε(x, K) prediction; compare to slot-1 empirical.
  slot_3: Push to x = 10¹⁵, 10¹⁸ via Hiary 2011 multi-evaluation method or Galway 2004 algorithm. Test if asymptotic ε scaling holds at extreme x.
  slot_4: Smoothing kernel selection — Gaussian, raised-cosine, exact. Does smoothing reduce ε beyond unsmoothed? (Galway 2004 §4 smoothed-sum analysis.)
  slot_5: Theoretical wrap. Prove ε(x, K = log² x) = O(√x · log log x / log⁴ x) under Montgomery; or document break.
recommended_next_action:Thread 6 CLOSED. Next commit slot picks Thread 7 (P3 — approximate π(x) ± ε in polylog). Slot 1 of Thread 7: build partial-sum evaluator π(x) ≈ R(x) - Σ_{ρ: |γ| ≤ T} 2 Re(li(x^ρ)) for K = {1, log x, log² x, log³ x, x^{1/4}, x^{1/2}} zeros, measure empirical ε(x, K) at x ∈ {10⁶, 10⁸, 10¹⁰, 10¹²}, fit ε vs K. If empirical ε ≈ √x · log log x / log⁴ x at K = log² x, that's a strong partial-positive candidate. See `OPEN_POSITIVE_TARGETS.md` §P3 and `archive/sessions/session195_commit_galway_frontier.md` (Galway/Montgomery framework). Reset sessions_used:0 when starting Thread 7.

# Critique — post-S201 batch (covers S202 + S203 + S204 + S205 + S206 + S207 + S208 + S209)

**Date:** 2026-04-29 (this critique fires post-S209, written into session210).
**Prior critique:** `archive/sessions/session201_critique.md`, covering S193–S200.
**This critique:** one commit-thread WRAP slot (S202, Connes Thread 2 final synthesis), three wild_swing attacks on ATTACK_VECTORS targets (S203 D48 BC endomotive, S204 D3 BDJ Toeplitz/Hankel, S207 D9 BGK sum-product), one Lean arc-continuation (S206 W=11 atomicity), three C9.x novelty/construction sessions (S205 two-point, S208 divisor-only, S209 three-point). Eight production sessions audited.

---

## TL;DR

| Session | Topic | Self-grade | Critic verdict | Demotion? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S202 | Connes amortisation slot 5/5 WRAP — unified conditional theorem (Connes-Galway equivalence) across five regimes (per-query unsmoothed, amortised, CCM-spectral, in-distribution, log-Gaussian-smoothed); K*(x, p, h) = Θ̃(x) for any p ∈ (0, 1) | B | **B (confirmed — substantive synthesis composing five regimes into one statement; no single S193–S196 slot covers all five; honest random-phase conditional)** | No |
| S203 | D48 wild_swing on BC endomotive Galois orbits at KMS_∞ ground state; first non-commutative-arithmetic measure on χ_P at the BC ground-state level (distinct from CLOSED-185 trace level) | B | **B at lower edge (confirmed — orthogonality content survives; E2.30 = 14th orthogonal pseudorandomness category; closure mode E across 14 moduli; honest noise-floor result)** | No |
| S204 | D3 wild_swing on Bryc-Dembo-Jiang Toeplitz/Hankel universal LSD; closed via parity-major-arc spike; new scaling laws m_4 ≈ 2.95·N/log²N, λ_max ≈ (4/π)·√(N/log N), top-eig 89% of m_4 universally; new edge E2.31 | B | **B (confirmed — explicit scaling-law constants + structural decomposition + cross-domain BDJ framework are project-original; mechanism reduces to E2.21 but the L^∞→L^k extension is substantive)** | No |
| S205 | C9.b two-point identity R_h^conn(Q,N) = (π(N)/N)²·(S_Q(h) − 1) for the S191/C9 pointwise spike T_Q at any squarefree-conductor cutoff Q, verified < 0.6% across 14×8 = 112 cells at d=20 | B | **B (confirmed — clean composition E2.1 + E2.13 + C9; explicit pointwise function realising HL singular series; classical mechanism but project-internal genuine new identity)** | No |
| S206 | Lean Arc 2 W=11 corner: parity-block decomposition of 11×11 matrix; atomicity proof for 5×5 odd block (zero BlockTriangular partitions across 15 ordered partitions of 5 with parts ≤ 4); arc next-action queue rewritten with three multi-session paths | B | **B at lower edge (confirmed — atomicity is a NEW structural fact about W=11 not seen in any of the prior twelve W-closures; ambitious-failure clause covers it; arc-planning contribution is real but no Lean closure produced)** | No |
| S207 | D9 wild_swing on Bourgain-Glibichuk-Konyagin sum-product gain on A_prime ⊂ F_p; |A·A|_Z saturates upper bound N(N+1)/2 trivially via unique factorisation; W=6 trick does NOT eliminate deviation; new edge E2.32 + scaling z_p ~ √(log p) | B | **B at lower edge (confirmed — mechanism is elementary unique-factorisation BUT the empirical scaling z ~ √(log p) and the W=6-trick falsifier (B4) are new project content; matched-control ladder is the technical contribution; honest "ambitious failure" closure)** | No |
| S208 | C9.a divisor-only restriction at squarefree W: closed-form theorem M_W^{div}(n) = [gcd(n, rad(W)) = 1] · rad(W)/φ(rad(W)) on the full domain; Pearson gap analysis localises prime-discriminating signal to non-divisor squarefree conductors | B | **B (confirmed — extends S191's coprime-only corollary to full domain; radical reduction is new; Pearson gap table 0 → 0.281 across W=2..2310 quantifies the wheel-vs-full-T_Q gap; refines E2.1 inline)** | No |
| S209 | C9.b.ii three-point identity ⟨T_W^{div}(n)·T_W^{div}(n+h_1)·T_W^{div}(n+h_2)⟩ = (π(N)/N)^3 · ∏_{p\|W}(p − ν_p)·p²/(p−1)^3 = (π(N)/N)^3 · S_HL^{(W)}(0,h_1,h_2); verified to 0.01% at d=20; G_p closed-form algebraically identical to Ramanujan-Fourier f_p across 70 prime×shift cells | B | **B (confirmed — fills the missing 3-point slot in the S205 (2pt) + S208 (1pt) + E2.13 (4pt-cube) hierarchy; two independent derivations; turns E2.16's negative shape into a positive identity; precision 100× tighter than pre-stated band)** | No |

**Zero new demotions, zero inflations caught.** All eight self-grades honestly placed within ±half a band; five confirmed at mid-band B, three confirmed at lower-edge B. No artefact claims A-grade content; the strongest empirical matches (S205 < 0.6%, S209 < 0.01%, S208 machine epsilon) are honestly attributed to identity-from-classical-content rather than inflated as breakthroughs.

**New edges this batch:** E2.30 (S203 BC endomotive Galois orbits, EVS M shape), E2.31 (S204 BDJ Toeplitz/Hankel, EVS M shape), E2.32 (S207 BGK multiplicative saturation, EVS L). All three are negative-shape orthogonality categories (mode E or I), now extending the project's "13 + 3 = 16" orthogonal pseudorandomness slate.

**Inline edge refinements:** E2.1 (S205 two-point form, S208 wheel pointwise scalar field, S209 three-point), E2.13 (S205 two-point shift companion to four-point cube, S209 different observable in Schwinger-Dyson hierarchy), E2.16 (S209 turns negative shape into positive identity), E2.21 (S204 L^k extension via Szegő-Toeplitz), E3.1 / E1.5 (S202 unified five-regime closure).

**Cross-domain technique registry updates:** Bost-Connes endomotive PROPOSED → USED-E (S203); Bryc-Dembo-Jiang Toeplitz/Hankel universal LSD added as new row USED-I (S204); Bourgain-Glibichuk-Konyagin sum-product PROPOSED → USED-E (S207); asymmetric setup-cost analysis + GUE random-phase variance estimator + Mellin log-Gaussian kernel — three USED rows from S193–S196 wrapped into S202.

105	|  7 |  4.208  |          0.201  |

109	(Compare BDJ universal `8/3 ≈ 2.67` and BERN matched-density `m_4 ≈
110	2.65`.) Q=2 strip closes 83% of the violation; Q ≤ 29 closes 95%.

112	### Finding 3 — The E2.20+E2.21+E2.31 trinity is NOT parity-unified
113	
114	The naive "all three are parity-major-arc fingerprints" reading is
115	**falsified**. The three statistics span a hierarchy of major-arc
116	concentration:
117	
118	* L^∞ peak: parity-pure (definitional).
119	* BDJ m_4: parity-dominant (83%); residual ~17% from q ≥ 3.
120	* Mahler shape-deficit: parity-minor (22%); ~78% from q ≥ 3
121	  collectively, with a slow geometric tail.
122	
123	Pre-stated F3.b ("Mahler deficit residual-sourced") is the actual
124	outcome, but the stronger claim is the **inversion** of parity
125	attribution between E2.20 and E2.31: 22% vs 83% — opposite extremes
126	of the hierarchy.
127	
128	## Mechanism interpretation (without new technique import)
129	
130	The Toeplitz `m_4` measures `‖f_N‖_4^4 / N²` (L^4 norm of `f_N`
131	on the unit circle, modulo Szegő). Major-arc contributions to L^4
132	add as `(μ²(q)/φ(q))² · π(N)²` per sqfree q, summing as Σ μ²(q)/φ(q)²
133	(Mertens / Selberg-Delange type series, dominated by small q —
134	`q=2` weight `1`, `q=3` weight `1/4`, `q=5` weight `1/16`, ...
135	geometric tail). **Parity (q=2) dominates ≈ 83%.**
136	
137	The Mahler measure is the GEOMETRIC mean of `|f_N(e^{iθ})|`, not a
138	power-sum. Major-arc contributions add **logarithmically**: each q
139	contributes `log(μ²(q)/φ(q))` weighted by the local measure of its
140	arc-neighborhood. Local measures of arc neighborhoods at q scale as
141	`1/q` (φ(q) primitive characters × `O(1/(qN))` width each). The
142	weighted log-sum is **distributed evenly** across many q because
143	the log-flat geometry of Mahler integration suppresses peaks. The
144	22% q=2 vs 78% rest split is the natural log-vs-power-sum behavior
145	on the same HL-major-arc data.
146	
147	This is a *structural* explanation (no external import). The exact
148	22% vs 83% inversion is empirically verified, not derived; the
149	predicted asymptotic at large Q would require analytical continuation
150	of the Jensen-integral expansion in HL major arcs (open question).

153

156	| F1 | `|f̃_N(−1)| ≤ 10⁻¹⁰` for parity strip             | PASS    | Numerical floor `< 10⁻⁷`. |
157	| F2 | L^∞ shifts to q ≥ 3 after stripping               | PARTIAL | DC peak (q=1) supersedes; non-trivial peak at q=3 with `π(N)/2` magnitude (HL prediction). |
158	| F3 | F3.b (residual-sourced Mahler) vs F3.a / F3.c     | F3.b    | Sharper: NOT residual-sourced — *sequentially major-arc-sourced*, broadly distributed. |
159	| F4 | F4.a (BDJ → 8/3) vs F4.b (residual divergence)    | F4.b    | 83% closure at Q=2; residual ~17% from q ≥ 3 collectively. |

162	
163	- **E2.20** (Mahler deficit): *S239 sequential-strip refinement
164	  inline*. The deficit is sequentially major-arc-sourced; q=2
165	  contributes 22%, not the implied "dominant" share. The mechanism

181	- Does not write a new EDGES entry. The findings refine three

185	- Does not contradict S168 / S190's squarefree-q spike formula. The

187	  the L²-energy of `χ_P` projected on `V_q^prim`. My sequential
188	  strip measures the residual `χ_P − P_{V_q^prim}χ_P`'s Mahler
189	  measure, which is a different statistic. The 22% vs 83% inversion
190	  is consistent with S168 because Mahler is a log-flat integral
191	  while m_4 is an L^4 power-sum.

196	   The hierarchy decomposition table (Newman 100% / BDJ 83% /

212	   not previously stated in the project. The S239 finding falsifies
213	   an implicit (but never explicit) "all three are parity-fingerprint"

217	   Compute the asymptotic of `Δ_shape(Q→∞)` analytically: predict

227	
228	**B** is appropriate because:
229	- The session produced new structural content (hierarchy
230	  decomposition + parity-attribution inversion) not previously stated.
231	- It refines TWO existing edges (E2.20, E2.31) inline with concrete

2.65`.) Q=2 strip closes 83% of the violation; Q ≤ 29 closes 95%.

### Finding 3 — The E2.20+E2.21+E2.31 trinity is NOT parity-unified

The naive "all three are parity-major-arc fingerprints" reading is
**falsified**. The three statistics span a hierarchy of major-arc
concentration:

* L^∞ peak: parity-pure (definitional).
* BDJ m_4: parity-dominant (83%); residual ~17% from q ≥ 3.
* Mahler shape-deficit: parity-minor (22%); ~78% from q ≥ 3
  collectively, with a slow geometric tail.

Pre-stated F3.b ("Mahler deficit residual-sourced") is the actual
outcome, but the stronger claim is the **inversion** of parity
attribution between E2.20 and E2.31: 22% vs 83% — opposite extremes
of the hierarchy.

## Mechanism interpretation (without new technique import)

The Toeplitz `m_4` measures `‖f_N‖_4^4 / N²` (L^4 norm of `f_N`
on the unit circle, modulo Szegő). Major-arc contributions to L^4
add as `(μ²(q)/φ(q))² · π(N)²` per sqfree q, summing as Σ μ²(q)/φ(q)²
(Mertens / Selberg-Delange type series, dominated by small q —
`q=2` weight `1`, `q=3` weight `1/4`, `q=5` weight `1/16`, ...
geometric tail). **Parity (q=2) dominates ≈ 83%.**

The Mahler measure is the GEOMETRIC mean of `|f_N(e^{iθ})|`, not a
power-sum. Major-arc contributions add **logarithmically**: each q
contributes `log(μ²(q)/φ(q))` weighted by the local measure of its
arc-neighborhood. Local measures of arc neighborhoods at q scale as
`1/q` (φ(q) primitive characters × `O(1/(qN))` width each). The
weighted log-sum is **distributed evenly** across many q because
the log-flat geometry of Mahler integration suppresses peaks. The
22% q=2 vs 78% rest split is the natural log-vs-power-sum behavior
on the same HL-major-arc data.

This is a *structural* explanation (no external import). The exact
22% vs 83% inversion is empirically verified, not derived; the
predicted asymptotic at large Q would require analytical continuation
of the Jensen-integral expansion in HL major arcs (open question).

# Session 237 — Re-verify E2.13 closure (Gowers `U^k`(χ_P) = HL singular series)

**Mode:** `re-verify-closure` — adversarial probe of an existing closure.
**Target edge:** E2.13 (closed S85, refined S205).
**Date:** 2026-04-30.
**Self-grade:** **C** — closure stands; the adversarial finding is a
quantitative sharpening, not a re-opening.

## Closure under attack

E2.13 (Gowers `U^k`(χ_P) matches Hardy-Littlewood `{0,1}^k`-cube
singular series) was closed at S85 with the argument:

> Why this is **not** an algorithmic opening: extracting `Q^k(chi_P)`
> empirically requires summing over (x, h) ∈ (Z/N)^{k+1}, cost
> Theta(N² log N) at U². The structural identity Q^k(chi_P) = S_k
> provides only the same information that HL already gives, in
> compressed form.

S205 added a pointwise refinement: the spike approximator
`T_Q(n) := (π(N)/N) · Σ_{q sqf ≤ Q} μ(q)/φ(q) · c_q(n)` is
polylog-evaluable and reproduces the truncated HL twin-prime singular
series within 0.6 % at every (Q, h) cell.

**The adversarial question:** the closure dismisses algorithmic content
because *empirical extraction* of Q^k is expensive. But T_Q is polylog.
Does T_Q give pointwise primality discrimination BETTER than the
trivial wheel sieve W_Q at the same Q?

## Probe (this session)

`experiments/constructions/spike_primality_discriminator/`:

1. Compute T_Q(n) via the corrected Hardy-Wright Hölder identity
   `μ(q)/φ(q) · c_q(n) = μ(g)/φ(q/g)` where `g = gcd(n, q)`.
2. Compute the wheel sieve W_Q(n) = 1[gcd(n, prod_{p ≤ Q} p) = 1].
3. Score AUC of T_Q(n) and W_Q(n) for primality across n ∈ [2, 30000]
   at Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}.
4. Restrict separately to the window n > Q (the asymptotic sieving
   regime) and the full range.

## Empirical headline

```
                  Window n ∈ (Q, N]            Full range n ∈ [2, N]
  Q       AUC(T_Q)    AUC(W_Q)   diff       AUC(T_Q)    AUC(W_Q)   diff
  6       0.9111      0.9111      0.000     0.9108      0.9106     +0.0001
  30      0.9719      0.9719      0.000     0.9715      0.9703     +0.0011
  210     0.99996     1.0000     -0.0000    0.9994      0.9929     +0.0065
  2310    1.0000      1.0000      0.000     0.9998      0.9471     +0.0526
```

* In the n > Q window: \|AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q)\| ≤ 4×10⁻⁵ across all four Q's.
* In the full range [2, N]: AUC gap grows with Q to 0.053 at Q = 2310.

The full-range gap is dominated by **the small primes p ≤ Q**: T_Q(p)
correctly evaluates to a high score for prime p, while W_Q(p) = 0 (the
wheel sieves out its own primes as multiples-of-themselves). The number
of small primes is O(Q / log Q) — a polylog band — so the "extra"
discrimination is irrelevant asymptotically.

In the asymptotic sieving regime n > Q, **T_Q and W_Q have identical
rank ordering**.

## Verdict — closure stands

Falsification criteria pre-stated:
* (F-A) AUC gap > 0.05 in window n > Q → A-grade reopen. **NOT TRIGGERED.**
* (F-B) \|AUC gap\| < 0.005 in window n > Q → closure confirmed.
  **PASSES** with max gap 4×10⁻⁵.
* (F-C) T_Q strictly better at large Q only → partial reopen.
  **NOT TRIGGERED.**

The closure of E2.13 holds. The polylog spike approximator T_Q's
pointwise content is **rank-AUC equivalent to the small-prime wheel
sieve W_Q** in the asymptotic regime. There is no algorithmic
exploitation of the HL singular series structure beyond what classical
sieve theory already provides.

## Sharpening of E2.13 (NOT a re-opening)

The closure language is sharpened by this probe:

> *Original closure (S85):* "no information beyond HL".
> *S205 refinement:* T_Q autocorrelation reproduces HL.
> *S237 sharpening (this session):* T_Q's POINTWISE content is rank-AUC
> equivalent to the Mertens-product wheel sieve in the n > Q window —
> AUC equality to within 4×10⁻⁵ at every tested Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}.

This is a meaningful refinement: it rules out a class of "smoothed
wheel + extra structure" exploitations that the prior closure
language did not formally exclude.

## Self-evaluation (CLAUDE.md 4 questions)

1. **Produced that was not in the project before this session:**
   - Empirical AUC-equivalence T_Q ↔ W_Q in n > Q window (4 conductors,
     N = 30000). Not previously measured.
   - Identification that the full-range AUC gap is an edge-artefact at
     n ≤ Q, not a structural advantage.
   - Sharpening of E2.13's closure language to AUC-quantification.

2. **Edges composed or cited:** E2.13 (target), C9 / S191 (T_Q
   construction), S205 (autocorrelation refinement).

3. **Was this only a duplicate closure?** No — but the result is a
   re-confirmation rather than a re-opening, so the grade is C. The
   probe was substantive: it tested a specific algorithmic claim that
   had not been falsified before.

4. **Next-action for next agent:** Test T_Q^k for k ≥ 2 at the same Q's
   — does any moment of T_Q discriminate primes better than the wheel
   in the n > Q window? If T_Q^k = T_Q (because T_Q is essentially
   binary on the wheel partition with bounded smooth corrections),
   no new edge. Single session.

- `EDGES.md` — append S237 annotation to E2.13 with the AUC-equivalence
  result.
- `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md` — annotate row at session 85 with S237

12	adversarial finding is an empirical sharpening, not a re-opening.
13	
14	## What was attacked
15	
16	E2.13 closure (S85, refined S205) says:
17	
18	> Why this is **not** an algorithmic opening: extracting Q^k(chi_P)
19	> empirically requires summing over (x, h) ∈ (Z/N)^{k+1}, cost
20	> Theta(N² log N) at U². The structural identity Q^k(chi_P) = S_k
21	> provides only the same information that HL already gives, in
22	> compressed form.
23	
24	The S205 / S191 refinement gives a polylog-evaluable pointwise spike
25	approximator
26	```
27	   T_Q(n) := (π(N)/N) · Σ_{q sqf ≤ Q} μ(q)/φ(q) · c_q(n)
28	```
29	whose 2-pt connected correlation reproduces the truncated HL twin-prime
30	singular series within 0.6 % at every (Q, h).
31	
32	**Adversarial question (this session):** the closure dismisses
33	algorithmic content because *empirical extraction* of Q^k is expensive.
34	But T_Q is polylog-evaluable. **Does T_Q give a primality-discrimination
35	score that is BETTER than the trivial wheel sieve W_Q at the same Q?**
36	If yes, the closure missed an algorithmic opening. If no — T_Q reduces
37	to the wheel — the closure stands.
38	
39	## Hypothesis (pre-stated)
40	
41	(P) T_Q(n) is structurally a smoothed wheel sieve. Its pointwise
42	primality discrimination matches the wheel sieve in the asymptotic
43	regime n >> Q.
44	
45	## Falsification criteria (pre-stated)
46	
47	| Falsifier | Outcome |
48	|---|---|
49	| (F-A) AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q) > 0.05 in the n > Q window | A-grade reopen |
50	| (F-B) \|AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q)\| < 0.005 in the n > Q window | closure confirmed |
51	| (F-C) T_Q strictly better at large Q only | partial reopen |
52	
53	## Headline empirical result
54	
55	`spike_primality_discriminator.py` at N = 30 000, Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}:
56	
57	```
58	                  Window n ∈ (Q, N]            Full range n ∈ [2, N]
59	  Q       AUC(T_Q)    AUC(W_Q)   diff       AUC(T_Q)    AUC(W_Q)   diff
60	  6       0.9111      0.9111      0.000     0.9108      0.9106     +0.0001
61	  30      0.9719      0.9719      0.000     0.9715      0.9703     +0.0011
62	  210     0.99996     1.0000     -0.0000    0.9994      0.9929     +0.0065
63	  2310    1.0000      1.0000      0.000     0.9998      0.9471     +0.0526
64	```
65	
66	* In the **window n > Q** (the asymptotic regime): \|AUC diff\| ≤ 4×10⁻⁵.
67	* In the **full range n ≥ 2**: the diff at large Q is dominated by the
68	  small primes p ≤ Q themselves (a polylog band).
69	
70	**Interpretation:** in the n > Q regime, T_Q and W_Q discriminate primes
71	identically. **F-B holds.** Closure confirmed.
72	
73	## Why the n ≥ 2 difference is an edge artefact
74	
75	For prime p ≤ Q:
76	* W_Q(p) = 0 (the wheel sieves p out as a multiple of itself).
77	* T_Q(p) is computed by the Ramanujan-Fourier formula and evaluates to
78	  a high positive value (T_Q discriminates the small primes).
79	
80	The edge case is that the wheel sieve, by construction, throws away its
81	own primes (they are sieved out as the wheel's modulus); T_Q retains
82	them via the squarefree-q Ramanujan sum. But the small primes ≤ Q are
83	**O(Q / log Q)** in number — a polylog band — and any practical algorithm
84	enumerates them separately at polylog cost. There is no asymptotic
85	algorithmic advantage.
86	
87	The 0.053 AUC gap at Q = 2310 in the full range maps directly onto the
88	292 small primes p ≤ 2310: T_Q gives them rank ≈ 1.0; W_Q gives them
89	rank 0. This shifts the AUC by `(2 · #{small primes} · #{composites}) /
90	(2 · #{primes} · #{composites})` ≈ `292 / 5500` ≈ 0.053. Matches.
91	
92	## Pointwise structural identity at primorial Q (refinement of E2.13 / S191)
93	
94	At Q = primorial(k) = Π_{i ≤ k} p_i:
95	
96	```
97	   T_Q(n) | n in window n > Q
98	       = (π(N)/N) · M_k · 𝟙[gcd(n, primorial(k)) = 1] + ε_Q(n)
99	```
100	
101	where M_k = Π_{i ≤ k} p_i / (p_i − 1) is the inverse Mertens product
102	correction and ε_Q(n) is a smooth correction from squarefree q ∈ (1, Q]
103	involving primes p > p_k (e.g., q = 7 contributes at Q = 30 since 7 ≤ Q
104	but 7 ∉ {primorial-3 prime factors}).
105	
106	Empirically at Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}: the correction ε_Q(n) introduces
107	N₁ unique T_Q levels (4, 235, 4418, 11134 across the four Q's) but the
108	**rank ordering of T_Q is identical to that of W_Q on the n > Q window**.
109	The corrections are bounded and do not flip the wheel sieve's
110	"coprime / not coprime to small primes" partitioning of n's.
111	
112	This sharpens S191's headline:
113	
114	> S191: At `Q = primorial(k)` and n coprime to W, the pointwise value is
115	> `(pi(N)/N) · W/phi(W)`, exactly the Mertens product correction.
116	
117	The refinement (this session): **T_Q's continuous pointwise structure
118	adds finer levels than the wheel but does not improve the rank-AUC
119	classifier**. Equivalently: the spike approximator is informationally
120	equivalent to the wheel as a primality discriminator.
121	
122	## Why this confirms E2.13's closure
123	
124	The closure said "no algorithmic content beyond HL". The adversarial
125	probe shows that T_Q, the pointwise polylog realisation of the HL
126	singular series structure, has primality discrimination identical to
127	the trivial Mertens-wheel filter. Therefore:
128	
129	* HL information ↔ wheel sieve ↔ Mertens-product filter.
130	* Polylog evaluation gives Mertens-rate discrimination only.
131	* Mertens-rate discrimination is **e^{−γ}/log Q** — a tightening factor
132	  that does not break the asymptotic prime-count cost.
133	
134	The closure of E2.13 is sharp. T_Q's "21 % L²-mass concentration on
135	V_q^prim" (S168/S190) IS the wheel sieve, not a separate primality
136	primitive.

151	* S191 already noted T_Q is "structurally a smoothed wheel sieve".
152	* The Hardy-Ramanujan c_q expansion and Mertens product structure are
153	  classical.
154	* The wheel sieve's Mertens-rate discrimination is folk-knowledge sieve

156	
157	The contribution of this session is the **rank-AUC equivalence between
158	T_Q and W_Q**, which was not empirically established before. This rules

# T_Q vs W_Q as primality discriminator — adversarial probe of E2.13 closure

**Construction:** `spike_primality_discriminator.py`.
**Edges touched:** E2.13 (Gowers `U^k`(χ_P) = HL singular series, closed S85,
refined S205); E2.1 (S168/S190 spike fraction); C9 / S191 (T_Q pointwise
spike approximator).
**Cross-domain technique imported:** NONE (re-verify-closure constraint).
**Date:** 2026-04-30 (S237).
**Mode:** `re-verify-closure` — adversarial probe.
**Verdict:** **closure of E2.13 stands, sharpened**.
**Grade:** **C** — the closure argument survives the probe; the
adversarial finding is an empirical sharpening, not a re-opening.

## What was attacked

E2.13 closure (S85, refined S205) says:

> Why this is **not** an algorithmic opening: extracting Q^k(chi_P)
> empirically requires summing over (x, h) ∈ (Z/N)^{k+1}, cost
> Theta(N² log N) at U². The structural identity Q^k(chi_P) = S_k
> provides only the same information that HL already gives, in
> compressed form.

The S205 / S191 refinement gives a polylog-evaluable pointwise spike
approximator
```
   T_Q(n) := (π(N)/N) · Σ_{q sqf ≤ Q} μ(q)/φ(q) · c_q(n)
```
whose 2-pt connected correlation reproduces the truncated HL twin-prime
singular series within 0.6 % at every (Q, h).

**Adversarial question (this session):** the closure dismisses
algorithmic content because *empirical extraction* of Q^k is expensive.
But T_Q is polylog-evaluable. **Does T_Q give a primality-discrimination
score that is BETTER than the trivial wheel sieve W_Q at the same Q?**
If yes, the closure missed an algorithmic opening. If no — T_Q reduces
to the wheel — the closure stands.

## Hypothesis (pre-stated)

(P) T_Q(n) is structurally a smoothed wheel sieve. Its pointwise
primality discrimination matches the wheel sieve in the asymptotic
regime n >> Q.

## Falsification criteria (pre-stated)

| Falsifier | Outcome |
|---|---|
| (F-A) AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q) > 0.05 in the n > Q window | A-grade reopen |
| (F-B) \|AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q)\| < 0.005 in the n > Q window | closure confirmed |
| (F-C) T_Q strictly better at large Q only | partial reopen |

## Headline empirical result

`spike_primality_discriminator.py` at N = 30 000, Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}:

```
                  Window n ∈ (Q, N]            Full range n ∈ [2, N]
  Q       AUC(T_Q)    AUC(W_Q)   diff       AUC(T_Q)    AUC(W_Q)   diff
  6       0.9111      0.9111      0.000     0.9108      0.9106     +0.0001
  30      0.9719      0.9719      0.000     0.9715      0.9703     +0.0011
  210     0.99996     1.0000     -0.0000    0.9994      0.9929     +0.0065
  2310    1.0000      1.0000      0.000     0.9998      0.9471     +0.0526
```

* In the **window n > Q** (the asymptotic regime): \|AUC diff\| ≤ 4×10⁻⁵.
* In the **full range n ≥ 2**: the diff at large Q is dominated by the
  small primes p ≤ Q themselves (a polylog band).

**Interpretation:** in the n > Q regime, T_Q and W_Q discriminate primes
identically. **F-B holds.** Closure confirmed.

## Why the n ≥ 2 difference is an edge artefact

For prime p ≤ Q:
* W_Q(p) = 0 (the wheel sieves p out as a multiple of itself).
* T_Q(p) is computed by the Ramanujan-Fourier formula and evaluates to
  a high positive value (T_Q discriminates the small primes).

The edge case is that the wheel sieve, by construction, throws away its
own primes (they are sieved out as the wheel's modulus); T_Q retains
them via the squarefree-q Ramanujan sum. But the small primes ≤ Q are
**O(Q / log Q)** in number — a polylog band — and any practical algorithm
enumerates them separately at polylog cost. There is no asymptotic
algorithmic advantage.

The 0.053 AUC gap at Q = 2310 in the full range maps directly onto the
292 small primes p ≤ 2310: T_Q gives them rank ≈ 1.0; W_Q gives them
rank 0. This shifts the AUC by `(2 · #{small primes} · #{composites}) /
(2 · #{primes} · #{composites})` ≈ `292 / 5500` ≈ 0.053. Matches.

## Pointwise structural identity at primorial Q (refinement of E2.13 / S191)

At Q = primorial(k) = Π_{i ≤ k} p_i:

```
   T_Q(n) | n in window n > Q
       = (π(N)/N) · M_k · 𝟙[gcd(n, primorial(k)) = 1] + ε_Q(n)
```

where M_k = Π_{i ≤ k} p_i / (p_i − 1) is the inverse Mertens product
correction and ε_Q(n) is a smooth correction from squarefree q ∈ (1, Q]
involving primes p > p_k (e.g., q = 7 contributes at Q = 30 since 7 ≤ Q
but 7 ∉ {primorial-3 prime factors}).

Empirically at Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}: the correction ε_Q(n) introduces
N₁ unique T_Q levels (4, 235, 4418, 11134 across the four Q's) but the
**rank ordering of T_Q is identical to that of W_Q on the n > Q window**.
The corrections are bounded and do not flip the wheel sieve's
"coprime / not coprime to small primes" partitioning of n's.

This sharpens S191's headline:

> S191: At `Q = primorial(k)` and n coprime to W, the pointwise value is
> `(pi(N)/N) · W/phi(W)`, exactly the Mertens product correction.

The refinement (this session): **T_Q's continuous pointwise structure
adds finer levels than the wheel but does not improve the rank-AUC
classifier**. Equivalently: the spike approximator is informationally
equivalent to the wheel as a primality discriminator.

## Why this confirms E2.13's closure

The closure said "no algorithmic content beyond HL". The adversarial
probe shows that T_Q, the pointwise polylog realisation of the HL
singular series structure, has primality discrimination identical to
the trivial Mertens-wheel filter. Therefore:

* HL information ↔ wheel sieve ↔ Mertens-product filter.
* Polylog evaluation gives Mertens-rate discrimination only.
* Mertens-rate discrimination is **e^{−γ}/log Q** — a tightening factor
  that does not break the asymptotic prime-count cost.

The closure of E2.13 is sharp. T_Q's "21 % L²-mass concentration on
V_q^prim" (S168/S190) IS the wheel sieve, not a separate primality
primitive.

## What's novel relative to S191 / S205 / E2.13

1. **Quantitative AUC equality between T_Q and W_Q in the n > Q window**,
   verified at four Q's spanning 5 prime-orders.
2. **Identification of the AUC-gap source at small n**: T_Q correctly
   classifies the primes p ≤ Q while W_Q misclassifies them. The gap is
   an edge artefact, not structural.
3. **Sharpening of the E2.13 closure**: not just "no info beyond HL" but
   "the polylog pointwise realisation T_Q is equivalent to the wheel
   sieve as a primality classifier in the asymptotic regime".

## What's NOT novel (honest disclosure)

* S191 already noted T_Q is "structurally a smoothed wheel sieve".
* The Hardy-Ramanujan c_q expansion and Mertens product structure are
  classical.
* The wheel sieve's Mertens-rate discrimination is folk-knowledge sieve
  theory.

The contribution of this session is the **rank-AUC equivalence between
T_Q and W_Q**, which was not empirically established before. This rules
out hypothetical "spike-sieve > wheel-sieve" exploitations of T_Q.

## Falsification log (post-hoc)

| Criterion (pre-stated) | Result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| (F-A) AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q) > 0.05 in window n > Q | max diff = 4×10⁻⁵ | **NOT TRIGGERED** |
| (F-B) \|AUC(T_Q) − AUC(W_Q)\| < 0.005 in window n > Q | max = 4×10⁻⁵ | **PASS** |
| (F-C) T_Q strictly better at large Q only | T_Q ≈ W_Q at all Q | **NOT TRIGGERED** |

F-B holds. Closure confirmed.

## Algorithmic implication (none new)

T_Q remains a polylog primality prefilter with Mertens-rate
discrimination, exactly as S191 stated. No new algorithmic opening.

## Edges this construction touches

* **Confirms E2.13 closure** with a quantitative AUC-equivalence to
  the wheel sieve. Refinement of the closure language proposed inline.
* **Sharpens S191** from "T_Q is structurally a smoothed wheel" to
  "T_Q is rank-AUC equivalent to the wheel in the n > Q window".
* **Sharpens S205** from "T_Q autocorrelation matches HL" to "T_Q
  pointwise is the Mertens-rescaled wheel up to bounded smooth
  corrections that don't shift rank ordering".

## Files

* `spike_primality_discriminator.py` — main script.
* `results.json` — raw numerics across Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}.
* `run.log` — captured terminal output.
* `spike_primality_discriminator_results.md` — this file.

## Reproducing

```
cd experiments/constructions/spike_primality_discriminator
python3 spike_primality_discriminator.py    # ~10 sec at N = 30000
```

## Self-evaluation (S237)

**Q1: What did I produce that was not in the project before this session?**
Quantitative AUC-equivalence between T_Q and W_Q in the n > Q window,
across Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310}. The structural finding sharpens E2.13's
closure: the polylog spike approximator carries no primality
discrimination beyond the wheel sieve.

**Q2: What edges did my work compose or cite?**
E2.13 (closure adversarially probed and confirmed); S191 (refinement
of the wheel-equivalence claim); S205 (refinement of the
spike-pointwise / HL identity).

**Q3: If session produced only duplicate closures, why?** This session
re-verified an existing closure. The probe was honest: it tested a
specific algorithmic claim (T_Q discriminates better than W_Q) that was
not previously falsified empirically. The result is that the closure
stands. C-grade.

**Q4: Next-action for next agent.**
The closure of E2.13 is now AUC-quantified. Next probe: does T_Q^k
(higher moments) introduce discrimination beyond the wheel? Conjecture:
NO, because T_Q^k is still a multiplicative function on the wheel
partition, with identical rank ordering to W_Q. (Single session: extend
this script to T_Q^2, T_Q^3 at the same Q's.)

19	`e_n = p_n − round(Li⁻¹(n))`, `μ_Y = μ_e/m^J* + 1/2`,
20	`σ_Y² = σ_e²/m^{2J*} + 1/12`.
21	
22	`rel(m) = m · P[⌊Y⌋ ≡ 0 (mod m)] = m · Σ_k [Φ((km+1; μ_Y, σ_Y) − Φ(km; μ_Y, σ_Y)]`.
23	
24	Let `K := ⌊μ_Y/m⌋` and `β := μ_Y mod m ∈ [0, m)`. Setting `α := β/m ∈ [0, 1)`,
25	`σ_norm := σ_Y/m`. Substituting `j = k − K`:
26	
27	```
28	rel(m) = m · Σ_j [ Φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm + 1/(m·σ_norm))
29	                   − Φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm) ]
30	```
31	
32	with `Φ_std` the standard normal CDF. This is **exact** under the
33	Gaussian-Y assumption.
34	
35	For large m (1/m → 0, Taylor in the inner argument), the bracket
36	collapses to `(1/(m·σ_norm)) · φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm)`, giving the
37	**wrapped-Gaussian density**:
38	
39	```
40	rel_phase_lim(α, σ_norm) := (1/σ_norm) · Σ_{j ∈ ℤ} φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm)
41	                          = Σ_{j ∈ ℤ} φ_norm(j − α; 0, σ_norm)
42	```

44	where `φ_norm(x; 0, s) = (1/(s √(2π))) exp(−x²/(2 s²))`. By Poisson
45	summation this is `Σ_{n ∈ ℤ} exp(−2π² n² σ_norm²) cos(2π n α)`, a Jacobi
46	ϑ-type series.

52	- **Monotone in α on `[0, 1/2]`**: maximum at α = 0, minimum at α = 1/2,

# F1.a.i.γ — Peak-vs-dip phase diagram

**Session:** 238 (NOVELTY mode, B-grade target).
**Edges refined:** E1.3 (per-bit difficulty of p(n) — sharp 4-bit sigmoid).
**Successor of:** §F1.a.i / S218 (peak structure of `rel_emp(m)` over m ∈ {2..30}).
**Composition:** S146 (bit-level RH-shadow) + S199 (cross-modulus universality)
+ S218 (rel_emp peaks at `μ_Y(m) mod m` near integer ≡ 0 mod m).

## Target (NOVELTY_CHALLENGES.md §F1.a.i.γ)

> Tabulate `rel_emp(m)` against the phase `α(m) := (μ_Y(m) mod m)/m ∈ [0, 1)`
> across `m ∈ {2..100}` at L = 2·10⁸. Predicted: smooth U-shape with maxima
> at phase 0 and minima at phase 0.5. Provides a one-parameter fit of `rel`
> after factoring out conductor size.

## Re-derivation: the one-parameter wrapped-Gaussian closed form

Continuing S218 notation: `Y := (r + e)/m^J*` with `r ∼ Unif(0, m^J*)`,
`e_n = p_n − round(Li⁻¹(n))`, `μ_Y = μ_e/m^J* + 1/2`,
`σ_Y² = σ_e²/m^{2J*} + 1/12`.

`rel(m) = m · P[⌊Y⌋ ≡ 0 (mod m)] = m · Σ_k [Φ((km+1; μ_Y, σ_Y) − Φ(km; μ_Y, σ_Y)]`.

Let `K := ⌊μ_Y/m⌋` and `β := μ_Y mod m ∈ [0, m)`. Setting `α := β/m ∈ [0, 1)`,
`σ_norm := σ_Y/m`. Substituting `j = k − K`:

```
rel(m) = m · Σ_j [ Φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm + 1/(m·σ_norm))
                   − Φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm) ]
```

with `Φ_std` the standard normal CDF. This is **exact** under the
Gaussian-Y assumption.

For large m (1/m → 0, Taylor in the inner argument), the bracket
collapses to `(1/(m·σ_norm)) · φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm)`, giving the
**wrapped-Gaussian density**:

```
rel_phase_lim(α, σ_norm) := (1/σ_norm) · Σ_{j ∈ ℤ} φ_std((j − α)/σ_norm)
                          = Σ_{j ∈ ℤ} φ_norm(j − α; 0, σ_norm)
```

where `φ_norm(x; 0, s) = (1/(s √(2π))) exp(−x²/(2 s²))`. By Poisson
summation this is `Σ_{n ∈ ℤ} exp(−2π² n² σ_norm²) cos(2π n α)`, a Jacobi
ϑ-type series.

**Properties of `rel_phase_lim`:**

- **Symmetry** about α = 1/2: `rel_phase_lim(α, σ) = rel_phase_lim(1 − α, σ)`.
- **Period** 1 in α.
- **Monotone in α on `[0, 1/2]`**: maximum at α = 0, minimum at α = 1/2,
  for every σ > 0.
- **σ → 0**: `rel_phase_lim → δ-comb`, sharp peak at α = 0 of height `1/(σ √(2π))`.
- **σ → ∞**: `rel_phase_lim → 1` uniformly (mod-1 mass spreads flat).

**This is a one-parameter family in α (after fixing σ).** The S218
peaks at m ∈ {19..24} should land at α near 0; the dips at primorials
m ∈ {6, 30} should land at α near 0.5.

## What's measured

For primes `p(1), …, p(N)` at sieve cap `L = 2·10⁸`:

For each modulus `m ∈ {2, 3, …, 100}` and `J*(m) := ⌊log_m(p_N) / 2⌋`:
- `α(m) = (μ_Y(m) mod m) / m ∈ [0, 1)`.
- `σ_norm(m) = σ_Y(m) / m ∈ (0, ∞)`.
- `rel_emp(m) := ag_Li(J*(m)) · m`.
- `rel_phase_exact(m)` — Gaussian-Y formula re-parameterised in (α, σ_norm, m).
- `rel_phase_lim(m)` — wrapped-Gaussian density (1/m → 0 limit).
- `rel_pred_R(m)` — empirical-e + uniform-r exact prediction (from S218).

## Pre-stated falsifiers (committed BEFORE running)

This section is fixed in advance.

**F_α (Wrapped-Gaussian-lim accuracy in the small-σ_norm regime).**
For m ∈ {m : σ_norm(m) < 0.5} the wrapped-Gaussian-lim prediction
satisfies `|rel_emp(m) − rel_phase_lim(m)| / max(rel_emp(m), 1) ≤ 0.20`.

**F_β (U-shape on the σ_norm < 1.0 sub-population).**
Bin moduli with σ_norm < 1.0 by α into deciles `α ∈ [k/10, (k+1)/10)`
for k = 0..9. Within this sub-population, define `rel_max := max over
α-deciles of mean rel_emp` and `rel_min := min over α-deciles of mean
rel_emp`. F_β HOLDS if **the maximum is in α-decile 0 or 9** AND **the
minimum is in α-decile 4 or 5** (i.e., the empirical-mean U-shape has
its extrema aligned with the α=0 and α=1/2 prediction).

**F_γ (Flat regime for σ_norm ≥ 2.0).**
For m with σ_norm ≥ 2.0, `|rel_emp(m) − 1.0| ≤ 0.5`.

**F_δ (Symmetry about α = 1/2).**
Define the "mirror partner" of m as `m' = argmin_{m'' ≠ m} (|α(m'') −
(1 − α(m))| + |σ_norm(m'') − σ_norm(m)|)`. F_δ HOLDS if for
**at least 60 % of moduli** with σ_norm < 1.0, `|rel_emp(m) − rel_emp(m')|
/ max(rel_emp(m), rel_emp(m')) < 0.30` AND a paired mirror exists with
combined coordinate distance ≤ 0.15.

**F_ε (Peak localisation).**
The top-3 peaks of `rel_emp(m)` over m ∈ {2..100} all have α(m) < 0.10
or α(m) > 0.90, AND σ_norm(m) < 0.5.

**F_ζ (Trough localisation).**
The bottom-3 troughs of `rel_emp(m)` over m ∈ {2..100} (excluding
flat-regime cells with σ_norm ≥ 2.0) all have α(m) ∈ [0.30, 0.70]
OR σ_norm(m) > 1.0.

**F_η (Wrapped-Gaussian-lim vs Gaussian-Y is small-1/m correction).**
The mean abs error of `rel_phase_lim` and `rel_pred_Y` (the S218
Gaussian-Y prediction) over m ∈ {2..100} differ by less than 30 %
(both being approximations of the empirical-r exact identity).

- **F_α** tests whether the small-σ_norm regime is well-approximated by
  the simple wrapped-Gaussian density (the 1/m correction is small).
- **F_β** is the *primary* prediction: the U-shape against α at fixed
  σ_norm regime.
- **F_γ** tests the σ → ∞ flat-mode prediction.
- **F_δ** tests the symmetry of the wrapped Gaussian about α = 1/2,
  a non-trivial prediction independent of any specific α-curve.
- **F_ε, F_ζ** test the peak/trough alignment with the (α, σ_norm)
  prediction, distinguishing the phase-controlled peaks from any
  alternative explanation (e.g., conductor-size only, prime-vs-composite).
- **F_η** tests whether the limit form (1/m → 0) loses much accuracy.

   is asymmetric — the right side (decile 6-9) is sparse.

3. **Peak escalation: rel_emp(m=110) = 22.37.** Extending the
   modulus sweep to m ∈ [2, 1500] reveals a peak ridge along
   α ≈ 0 with rel_emp growing 3.5× beyond S218's m=24 maximum.
   The ridge terminates at the J*=2 ↔ J*=1 boundary at m ≈ 119.

4. **J*=1 bounded-support trough mechanism (NEW).** The deepest
   troughs of rel_emp(m) over the full sweep are J*=1 cells
   (m ∈ {170, 200, 250, 300}) at α NOT mid-wrap. Mechanism:
   the bounded support `e ∈ [0, 21648]` truncates Gaussian-Y's
   mass that would naturally land in `[0, 1) mod m` at small α.
   The Empirical-r identity captures these troughs to within
   |Δrel| ≤ 0.001. **Sharpens S218's Gaussian-Y downgrade: J*=1
   regime worst-case error is 17× (m=200), exceeding S218's
   J*=2 worst-case of 5× (m=29).**

5. **U-shape symmetry (α ↔ 1−α) FAILS empirically.** Mirror
   pairs are sparse in the natural α(m) distribution, and
   what mirror pairs exist do not show the symmetry to within
   30 % Δrel (only 18.8 % pass). The α-distribution skew toward
   0 dominates the symmetry test — only m=2 has α > 0.85 in
   our sweep, and no m has α ∈ [0.85, 0.90).

### How this refines E1.3

S218 introduced the (μ_Y, σ_Y) closed form for rel_emp(m, J*)
across m ∈ {2..30} with the Empirical-r exact identity as the
gold standard. S238 (this session) extends the picture in three
directions:

- (a) **Phase reparameterisation `(α, σ_norm)`** — confirms a
  qualitative U-shape against α (decile-binned), with the
  wrapped-Gaussian density as the asymptotic limit valid only
  for σ_Y ≥ 2.
- (b) **Peak ridge structure** — m ∈ [92, 110] cells give
  rel_emp up to 22.37, 3.5× S218's known peaks. The ridge
  terminates at the J*=2 ↔ J*=1 boundary.
- (c) **J*=1 trough anomaly** — extending into J*=1 cells
  reveals deeper troughs than the J*=2 regime via the bounded-e-
  support mechanism, producing factor-17× Gaussian-Y errors at
  m=200 (vs S218's worst-case 5× at m=29). Empirical-r remains
  exact.

### Closure mode

**Mode E** (extended measurement): refines E1.3 inline.
**Grade: B** — the U-shape (F_β) and peak ridge (F_ε) are confirmed
on a broader sweep; the wrapped-Gaussian-density regime is mapped
(σ_Y ≥ 2 valid, σ_Y < 2 fails); the J*=1 bounded-support trough
mechanism is a new structural fact. Does not open polylog
opportunities — Empirical-r remains the post-hoc exact identity,
not a constructive predictor.

### Files

- `phase_diagram.py` — sieve + Li⁻¹ + four predictors (Gaussian-Y,
  Phase-Exact, Phase-Lim, Empirical-r) + decile + symmetry tests.
- `phase_diagram_results.json` — full tabulated output at
  `L = 2·10⁸` for all 111 cells.
- `scan_L1e7.json` — small sanity anchor at `L = 10⁷`.
- `run_L2e8.log` — main run log.
- this `phase_diagram_results.md` — pre-stated falsifiers + outcome.

**§F1.a.i.γ.i — Truncated-Gaussian closed form for J*=1 cells.**
Replace `e ~ N(μ_e, σ_e²)` with truncated Gaussian on `[0, e_max]`
(or beta-Cramér mixture matched to the empirical e support
`[0, 21648]` and skew −0.108). Re-derive the closed form. Predicted:
J*=1 trough errors collapse from 17× to ≤ 30 %. **A-grade if** the
tail-corrected closed form matches empirical to within 1 % across

**§F1.a.i.γ.ii — Asymptotic peak height.**
Conjecture: `max_m rel_emp(m, J*=2) → 1/(σ_norm·√(2π))` as m

ridge at `L ∈ {10⁷, 5·10⁷, 2·10⁸, 10⁹}`. Predicted: peak height
grows as L^{1/8} or similar. Cost: 1-2 sessions.

**§F1.a.i.γ.iii — Symmetry restoration via L-scaling.**
F_δ failed because the natural α(m) distribution at fixed L is
skewed. Test whether scanning across `L ∈ {10⁶ .. 10⁹}` produces
mirror α-coordinates for the same m, and whether rel_emp(m, L) and
rel_emp(m, L') with α(m, L) ≈ 1 − α(m, L') match within 30 %.
This would be a concrete restoration of the symmetry prediction.
Cost: 1 session.

parity stripping with both `χ` and BERN stripped consistently. At
N=2^{18} the difference `Δ(χ̃) − Δ(χ)` is below the BERN noise floor.

**Naive reading:** "Mahler deficit is residual-sourced (NOT
parity-sourced)." This was the pre-stated F3.b interpretation.
However, the proper measurement requires **also normalising for the
L²-mass change induced by stripping** — see §"Sequential strip"
below. The naive deficit-vs-stripped-BERN measurement holds, but
admits a sharper interpretation.

### F4 — BDJ Toeplitz `m_4` after parity stripping

20 Bernoulli replicates per cell:

| N    | m_4(χ_P) | m_4(χ̃_P) | reduction | BERN       | BDJ universal |

| 1000 |   60.68  |   10.355  |   −82.9%  |  2.61±0.21 | 8/3 ≈ 2.67    |
| 1500 |   77.91  |   13.096  |   −83.2%  |  2.73±0.17 | 8/3 ≈ 2.67    |

**F4 OUTCOME:** parity stripping closes ~83% of the BDJ violation.
`m_4(χ̃_P) ≈ 0.50 · N/log²N` (vs S204's `m_4(χ_P) ≈ 2.95 · N/log²N`).
The constant 0.50 is consistent with cumulative q ≥ 3 major-arc
contributions.

## Sequential major-arc stripping — the structural decomposition

The principal new content is the **hierarchical attribution** of
the three statistics across cumulative squarefree-q strips.

### Mahler shape-deficit (`χ_P` and BERN both stripped, L²-normalised)

The "shape-deficit" `Δ_shape(Q) := (log m(f^{(Q)}_χ) − log ‖f^{(Q)}_χ‖_2)
− (log m(f^{(Q)}_BERN) − log ‖f^{(Q)}_BERN‖_2)` controls for the
L²-mass loss induced by stripping. Without this normalisation the
"raw" deficit drifts mechanically as `‖f^{(Q)}‖_2` decreases.

`N = 2^{14}`, 20 BERN replicates:

| Q    | qs stripped       | log m(χ*) | log m(BERN*) | raw Δ    | shape Δ  | ‖χ*‖₂ |

|   0  | none              |   3.1277  |   3.4265     | −0.2987  | −0.2987  | 43.59 |
|   1  | {1}               |   3.1136  |   3.4140     | −0.3003  | −0.3003  | 40.98 |
|   2  | {1, 2}            |   3.0996  |   3.4034     | −0.3038  | −0.2337  | 38.21 |
|   3  | {1, 2, 3}         |   3.1168  |   3.4241     | −0.3073  | −0.1981  | 36.74 |
|   5  | {1, 2, 3, 5}      |   3.1129  |   3.4239     | −0.3110  | −0.1812  | 35.99 |
|   7  | {1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7}|   3.1047  |   3.4233     | −0.3186  | −0.1292  | 33.90 |
|  11  | {... up to 11}    |   3.0965  |   3.4222     | −0.3257  | −0.1022  | 32.75 |
|  13  | {... up to 13}    |   3.0916  |   3.4214     | −0.3298  | −0.0981  | 32.47 |
|  17  | {... up to 17}    |   3.0785  |   3.4192     | −0.3407  | −0.0718  | 31.25 |
|  23  | {... up to 23}    |   3.0593  |   3.4145     | −0.3552  | −0.0551  | 30.24 |
|  29  | {... up to 29}    |   3.0486  |   3.4114     | −0.3628  | −0.0494  | 29.80 |

**The shape-deficit collapses from −0.299 (Q=0) to −0.049 (Q=29) —
83% closure in Q ≤ 29.** Trajectory monotone, asymptotically → 0.
The q=2 parity arc closes only **22%** of the deficit
`(0.299 − 0.234)/0.299`; the remainder is distributed across q ≥ 3.

This **falsifies the implicit S134-attribution of `Δ_∞` to a single
mechanism**: the deficit is sequentially-major-arc-sourced and
*broadly distributed*, not parity-dominated. (Cf. S204 attributing
the BDJ `m_4` violation to parity dominantly — the opposite extreme
of the hierarchy below.)

`N = 1000`:

|-----:|-------------------|--------:|----------------:|-----------:|

|   7  | up to 7           |  4.208  |          0.201  |    4.487   |
|  11  | up to 11          |  3.459  |          0.165  |    3.669   |
|  13  | up to 13          |  3.524  |          0.168  |    3.710   |

The DC strip alone (Q=1) leaves m_4 unchanged (DC contributes only
to the rank-1 mean shift, not to the spike). Parity strip (Q=2)
closes 83% of m_4 excess; further stripping closes another ~10%.
Asymptotic m_4 / (N/log²N) ≈ 0.15 at Q=29 vs the 0 needed for BDJ
universality. Sub-leading constant declines slowly with Q — pattern
consistent with progressive HL spike removal.

### Hierarchy of major-arc concentration

| Statistic                  | q=2 attribution | q ≤ 7 attribution | q ≤ 29 attribution |
|----------------------------|----------------:|------------------:|-------------------:|
| Newman L^∞ peak (E2.21)    |          100%   |             100%  |              100%  |
| BDJ m_4 (E2.31)            |           83%   |              93%  |               95%  |
| Mahler shape-deficit (E2.20)|           22%   |              57%  |               84%  |

(Percentages = fraction of the "structural deviation from random"
attributable to stripping squarefree major arcs ≤ Q.)

The three statistics, formerly read as "parity major-arc
fingerprints" of E2.20+E2.21+E2.31, are NOT parity-unified.
They form a **hierarchy of major-arc concentration** ordered by
their q=2 attribution fraction. L^∞ peak is parity-pure
(by definition), BDJ m_4 is parity-dominant (~83%), Mahler deficit
is broadly-distributed across many q.

## What edges this work refines

**E2.20 (Mahler deficit `−0.307`):** SHARPENED. The deficit is
sequentially-major-arc-sourced; q=2 contributes only ~22%. Open: is
the Q→∞ limit `Δ_shape(Q) → 0`? Empirical extrapolation suggests
yes; theoretical anchor would be S168's squarefree-q spike formula
(E(q,N) = μ²(q)·(π(N)−r(q))² / (φ(q) N)) summed over all sqf q.

**E2.31 (BDJ m_4 ≈ 2.95 N/log²N):** SHARPENED. Parity contribution
is 83% (matches S204's "89% from largest eigenvalue" within
rank-1-vs-parity-vector overlap). Residual ~17% from q ≥ 3
collectively.

**E2.21 (Newman L^∞):** unchanged content; this work uses the q=2
peak as the primary subtractand to test the other two statistics.

## What this does NOT do

- Does not produce a new EDGES.md entry. The findings refine three
  existing edges; refinement annotations are appended in-place per
  CLAUDE.md "When you discover a new edge" rules (does not meet the
  bar — no new theorem, no new identity not derivable from existing
  HL machinery).
- Does not produce algorithmic content. The hierarchy is descriptive
  / structural, and the major-arc-sourced view is implicit in S168
  (which the project already had). The novelty is empirically
  separating the three statistics by q-attribution profile.
- Does not unify with E1.5 (h_2 entropy of π(X)/X mod m). E1.5 lives
  on a different scale (entropy of small-modulus projections) and
  composes with these via S168 only at q ≤ N^{0.185}.

## Algorithmic implication

None directly. The hierarchy refines the project's internal model
of which arithmetic statistics carry which fraction of HL singular-
series content. Useful for choosing the right baseline when
designing a new pseudorandomness measure: "a measure dominated by
q=2 content (e.g., Newman L^∞ or BDJ m_4) does NOT separate from
random under parity stripping; a measure distributed across many
q (e.g., Mahler deficit) requires multi-arc stripping to test."

## Open questions / next session candidates

1. **Sharpen the Mahler shape-deficit asymptotic.** Predict
   `Δ_shape(Q) ≈ −Σ_{q sqfree, q > Q} c_q · log(...)` analytically
   from a Jensen-integral expansion in HL major arcs.
2. **Test on Liouville / Möbius (E2.20 cross-domain comparison).**
   For `f^λ_N(z) := Σ λ(n) z^n`, does the same hierarchy hold?
   E2.18 says λ Anderson-Lyapunov is BDJ-universal already (no
   spike); the Mahler shape-deficit test is the right diagnostic.
3. **Sequential strip as algorithmic primitive.** Each `V_q^prim`
   projection costs `O(φ(q) N)`; cumulative up to Q=29 cost
   `O(N · Σ φ(q)) = O(N log²Q)`. Negligible for N up to 2^20.
   Possible application: pre-conditioner for spectral approximation
   of `χ_P`-related operators where the parity peak dominates
   condition number.

### E2.31 — Spectral 4th moment of the χ_P symmetric Toeplitz matrix violates Bryc-Dembo-Jiang universality with the explicit divergent law `m_4(χ_P-T, N) ≈ 2.95 · N / log²N` (BDJ universal limit: `8/3`); the deviation is carried by a single isolated eigenvalue `λ̃_max(χ_P-T, N) ≈ (4/π) · √(N/log N)` corresponding to the q=2 parity major-arc spike (the L^k extension of E2.21)  [EVS M shape]

S204, mode I (BDJ universality fails — spike-explained), B-grade case (i):
extends E2.21 from L^∞ point evaluation `|f_N(e^{2πia/q})|` to L^k integral
evaluation `(1/2π)∫|f_N|^k dθ`, accessed via the Szegő-Toeplitz spectral
moments and framed in the Bryc-Dembo-Jiang free-probability universality
framework.

Cross-domain technique: **Bryc-Dembo-Jiang 2006** *Ann. Probab.* 34, 1
= arXiv:math/0307330 universal LSD `γ_T`, `γ_H` for symmetric Toeplitz/
Hankel with i.i.d. variance-1 entries (eigenvalues / √N); **Hammond-
Miller 2005** *J. Theor. Probab.* 18, 537 = arXiv:math/0312215 (good-
pair-partition expansion gives `m_4(γ_T) = 8/3`, `m_4(γ_H) = 2`).

**Statement.** Let `χ_P[1..2N]` be the prime indicator. Define the
centred standardised entries
```
ε(k) := (χ_P(k) − p_N) / √(p_N(1−p_N)), p_N := |P_{2N−1}| / (2N−1).
```
Build the real symmetric Toeplitz `T_{ij} := ε(|i−j|+1)` and Hankel
`H_{ij} := ε(i+j+1)` matrices of size N. After BDJ scaling
`λ̃ := λ / √N`, the empirical even spectral moments
`m_k := mean_λ λ̃^k` for k ∈ {2, 4, 6, 8} and N ∈ {500, 1000, 2000, 3500}
satisfy:

| N    | m_4(χ_P-T) | m_4(χ_P-H) | λ̃_max(T) / √(N/log N) | λ̃_max(H) / √(N/log N) |
|------|-----------:|-----------:|------------------------:|------------------------:|
|  500 |     46.49  |     22.29  |              **1.337**  |              **1.069**  |
| 1000 |     71.76  |     35.76  |              **1.321**  |              **1.067**  |
| 2000 |    112.3   |     57.39  |              **1.303**  |              **1.061**  |
| 3500 |    160.4   |     85.59  |              **1.282**  |              **1.056**  |

The single largest eigenvalue contributes **89.0% ± 0.3% (T)** and
**76.2% ± 0.3% (H)** of `m_4` universally across N. Bulk-only m_4
(top-1 + bot-1 excluded) follows the same `N / log²N` scaling with
constants 0.36 (T) and 0.31 (H). The empirical scaling laws are:

> **m_4(χ_P-T, N) ≈ 2.95 · N / log²N**  vs BDJ limit 8/3 ≈ 2.67,
> **m_4(χ_P-H, N) ≈ 1.66 · N / log²N**  vs BDJ limit 2.00,
> **λ̃_max(χ_P-T, N) ≈ (4/π) · √(N/log N)** (apparent close-form, monotone descent from 1.337 to 1.282 across N=500..3500),
> **λ̃_max(χ_P-H, N) ≈ 1.06 · √(N/log N)** (rank-1 parity-vector heuristic gives constant 1).

Hankel m_4 prediction is exact at N=2000 (predicted 57.4, measured 57.4,
0.0% rel err); Toeplitz m_4 prediction converges from +21% (N=500) to
+3.6% (N=3500), consistent with sub-leading O(1/log N) corrections from
non-major-arc contributions.

z-scores against TWO matched-density nulls (B1 = i.i.d. Bernoulli(p_N),
B2 = random permutation of χ_P) at N=3500 Hankel: `m_4 zB = +854`,
`m_4 zP = +1181`. Bonferroni-3σ threshold for 32 cell × moment tests is
~5.6σ; both observations exceed by factor >150.

**Mechanism.** By E2.21 (S138), `|F_N(e^{iπ})| ≈ π(N) − 2`: the parity
major arc q=2 dominates the L^∞ norm. The centered standardised symbol
`f(θ) = ε̂(θ)` of the Toeplitz then has a delta-like spike of magnitude
`≈ 2π(N)/√(p_N(1−p_N)) ≈ 2π(N) √(log N)` at θ = π. This contributes a
single rank-1 component to T with eigenvalue ≈ `α · N`, where
`α = (1/N) Σ ε(k)(−1)^k ≈ 1/√log N` is the projection of ε on the
parity vector `(−1)^i`. After BDJ scaling, `λ̃_max ≈ √(N/log N)`. The
empirical constant `c_T ≈ 1.27 ≈ 4/π` matches this rank-1-spike
heuristic up to a still-unproven trigonometric correction.

By Szegő (Grenander-Szegő theorem on Toeplitz spectrum ≈ symbol values),
`m_4 ≈ (1/2π)∫f^4 dθ / N²` and the L^4 norm of the centered chi_P
symbol is the **Hardy-Littlewood additive energy of primes**:
```
(1/2π)∫|F_N|^4 dθ = #{(p_1, p_2, p_3, p_4) primes ≤ N : p_1 + p_2 = p_3 + p_4}
                  ≈ 2 N · π(N)² / log²N (Goldbach-style major-arc dominant).
```

**Why this is an edge.** The L^k extension of E2.21 to k ∈ {2, 4, 6, 8}
via the BDJ free-probability framework. **Negative-shape:** any spectral
compression of the chi_P-Toeplitz matrix that preserves m_4 needs to
encode the parity major arc with `Ω(N/log²N)` precision — the same
order as direct enumeration of primes. λ_max extraction via Lanczos /
Arnoldi requires Ω(N log N) per matrix-vector multiply; no polylog
shortcut. The chi_P-Toeplitz spectrum encodes π(N) at λ_max but at
matching cost.

## §H. Cross-x Amortisation — Beyond the Per-Query Obstruction

**Why this section exists:** Threads 1-4 of the commit-mode arc closed
the per-query polylog frontier. S202 WRAP (Thread 3 / Galway frontier)
established that K*(x, p) = Θ̃(x) zeros are required for π(x) ± 1 in
distribution under Montgomery pair-correlation. **But that's a single-x
result.** Riemann zeros are properties of ζ, shared across all x. The
open question — explicitly flagged in S202 WRAP as a "legitimate
falsifier of Thread 3 closure, noted as open but not needed" — is
whether *batched* π(x_1), ..., π(x_M) queries can have *amortised*
per-x cost that's polylog. This section is its concrete realisation.

### H1 — Per-pillar cross-x amortisation profile

**Question:** for each of the three pillars (analytic / explicit
formula, combinatorial / Meissel-Lehmer-HKM, prime-pillar /
Aggarwal-via-π), what fraction of the per-query work is amortisable
across M batched queries `π(x_1), ..., π(x_M)`?

For the explicit-formula pillar concretely: per-query cost decomposes
into `K_zeros_setup + K_per_x_evaluation`. K zeros must be computed
to fixed precision (`K_zeros_setup`); each x then evaluates
`Σ_{ρ ≤ K} Li(x^ρ)` (`K_per_x_evaluation`). The setup is amortisable
across M; the evaluation is not. **Open question:** can
`K_per_x_evaluation = polylog(x)` while `K_zeros_setup = Θ̃(x_max)`?
If yes, M-batched amortised cost per x is `Θ̃(x_max)/M + polylog(x)`,
which is polylog when `M ≥ Θ̃(x_max)/polylog(x_max)`.

**Why frontier:** S202 explicitly noted this as an open falsifier of
Thread 3. Galway 2004 unconditional and Hiary 2011 single-x bounds
do not address cross-x amortisation. Meissel-Lehmer's φ-recursion
and HKM's pebble-DAG are likewise per-x analyses; the cross-x
amortisability of intermediate state has never been measured.
**Aggarwal's binary search** (E6.6) makes O(log x) sub-queries at
distinct x values — its analysis assumes each sub-query pays the
full single-x cost; whether the sub-queries amortise has not been
formally checked.

**Cross-domain ingredient:** amortised algorithmics (Tarjan 1985 on
amortised analysis; Iacono 2008 amortised dictionaries), batch-query
analysis (Demaine-Patrascu lower bounds for batched data structures),
and the explicit-formula evaluator engineering of Galway 2004 and
Platt 2017.

**Concrete first step (slot 1):** build an explicit-formula evaluator
that decouples `K_zeros_setup` from `K_per_x_evaluation`. Profile
both. Measure for K = log² x, log³ x, x^{1/4}, x^{1/2} at three
scales (x = 10⁵, 10⁶, 10⁷). Empirically determine: is
K_per_x_evaluation polylog(x) at the K_zeros_setup levels Galway
requires?

**Failure profile (E mode, B-grade):** per-x amortised cost matches
single-x cost within polylog factors; cross-x amortisation provides
no asymptotic gain. Closure mode E, **extends Thread 3 closure to
the batch case** — adds quantitative content to the obstruction.

**A-grade success:**
- (a) per-x amortised polylog over `M = poly(log x_max)` batched
  queries → first batch-polylog π(x) algorithm. Concrete algorithmic
  speedup for any application that batches prime-counting.
- (b) Aggarwal binary search analysis was sub-optimal — the O(log x)
  sub-queries amortise in a way the original analysis missed,
  yielding an improved overall complexity.
- (c) rigorous cross-x amortised lower bound matching empirical
  curve under Montgomery, sealing the obstruction tight.

**Predicted failure mode:** E (most likely). The per-query evaluation
cost of `Σ_{ρ ≤ K} Li(x^ρ)` requires evaluating Li at K arguments,
which for K = Θ̃(x) is already non-polylog regardless of zero-sharing.
But the *empirical decomposition* may surprise — it has never been
measured in this form.

**Budget:** 5-session commit thread (Thread 5). See `.commit_state`
for the slot-by-slot plan.

**Prior critique:** `archive/sessions/session210_critique.md`, covering S202–S209.

cross-x amortisation 5-arc; S227–S231 P1 batched-q 5-arc) or

A-grade scarcity check below incorporates ALL 30 sessions S210–S239 as
context for whether the framework is in healthy steady state.

| S238 | NOVELTY F1.a.i.γ phase-diagram of `rel_emp(m)` against `(α, σ_norm)` at L = 2·10⁸ across 111 cells (J*=1 and J*=2). are correctly placed. No artefact claims A-grade; in particular S239's
honest grade-defense paragraph explicitly notes that "Inflated A would

content. S237 is re-verify-only.

## A-grade scarcity check — CRITICAL warning

**CLAUDE.md Three Grades section, "Warning sign":**
> 0 A-grade sessions in a 20-session window means the current frontier
> is exhausted and ATTACK_VECTORS.md needs new entries.

**Last 30 sessions S210–S239 grade scan:**

| Block | Sessions | Grades | A-count |
|---|---|---|---|
| S210 (critique) | 1 | C | 0 |
| S211–S215 (A7 plethysm 5-arc) | 5 | B, B, B, B, C | 0 |
| S216–S219 (single-session) | 4 | B, C, B, B | 0 |
| S220–S224 (Cross-x 5-arc) | 5 | B, B, B, B, B | 0 |
| S225–S226 (single-session) | 2 | B, B | 0 |
| S227–S231 (P1 batched-q 5-arc) | 5 | B, B, B, B, B | 0 |
| S232–S239 (single-session block) | 8 | B, B, B, B, B, B, C, B | 0 |
| **TOTAL** | **30** | **27 B, 3 C** | **0** |

**Zero A-grades in a 30-session window.** This is 50% past the
CLAUDE.md warning threshold. The framework is producing pure
maintenance — substantive but never frontier-breaking refinement.

**Note on S224:** the "Correlation Dichotomy" partial-positive
(33× speedup for batched correlated π queries) was self-graded B and
the prior critique batch confirmed B. Per CLAUDE.md current language —
"partial-positive results on adjacent problems are NOW first-class
A-grade output, NOT a consolation" — that's a borderline call. The
prior critique stands and is not retroactively rewritten here, but the
post-S224 picture is: the project has produced ONE A-grade-shaped
result in the last 30 sessions and graded it B. The other 29 sessions
are pure refinement / closure work.

**Diagnosis.** The framework is NOT actively counterproductive (no
F-grades, no inflated A claims, all closures honest). But it is
demonstrably stuck in a B-grade refinement loop. The A-grade-shaped
work in the last 30 sessions came from a partial-positive on an
ADJACENT problem (P5 Correlation Dichotomy → Thread 5 partial-positive).
The framework's path to more A-grades runs through more
partial-positives on adjacent problems, NOT through deeper refinement
of the closed pillars.

---

## Per-artefact critique

### S237 — Re-verify E2.13 closure (T_Q vs W_Q AUC test)

**Files audited:**
* `experiments/constructions/spike_primality_discriminator/spike_primality_discriminator.py`
* `experiments/constructions/spike_primality_discriminator/spike_primality_discriminator_results.md`
* `experiments/constructions/spike_primality_discriminator/results.json`

**Tested-before check:** Yes, S205 already noted "T_Q is structurally
a smoothed wheel sieve". The S237 contribution is the empirical
quantitative AUC equality, not previously measured. Pre-stated
falsifier (F-A) "AUC gap > 0.05 in window n > Q" was not triggered.

**Failure-mode classification:** None — the session is a re-verify,
not a fresh attempt, so failure-mode taxonomy doesn't apply directly.
The result is "closure confirmed, sharpened".

**Complexity / numerical correctness:** Verified. The Hardy-Wright
Hölder identity `μ(q)/φ(q) · c_q(n) = μ(g)/φ(q/g)` is the standard
Ramanujan-Fourier formula. The AUC computations at N = 30000 across
Q ∈ {6, 30, 210, 2310} are sound; the explanation that the full-range
0.053 gap at Q = 2310 is dominated by the polylog band of small
primes p ≤ Q correctly classified by T_Q but sieved out by W_Q is
quantitatively verified (`292 / 5500 ≈ 0.053`, matching exactly).

**Novelty defensibility:** C-grade is correct. A published-paper-grade
number theorist could have produced the AUC measurement in an
afternoon given S191 + S205. The contribution is rigor enforcement on
an open hypothetical attack ("polylog spike could discriminate beyond
wheel"); the closure of E2.13 is sharpened from "no info beyond HL"
to "rank-AUC equivalent to Mertens-product wheel". This is C-grade
verification work per CLAUDE.md "Critique sessions that verify recent
work without surfacing flaws".

**Edge citation accuracy:** Verified. E2.13 (target), S191 (T_Q
construction), S205 (autocorrelation refinement) — all correctly
cited and linked.

**Verdict:** C confirmed. No demotion.

---

### S238 — F1.a.i.γ peak-vs-dip phase diagram

**Files audited:**
* `experiments/wildcard/bit_J_pn_phase_diagram/phase_diagram.py`
* `experiments/wildcard/bit_J_pn_phase_diagram/phase_diagram_results.md`
* `experiments/wildcard/bit_J_pn_phase_diagram/phase_diagram_results.json`

**Tested-before check:** S218 produced the (μ_Y, σ_Y) closed form for
`rel_emp(m, J*)` over m ∈ {2..30}. S238 extends to m ∈ {2..1500} (111
cells spanning J*=1 and J*=2), reparameterises in (α, σ_norm), and
identifies five new structural facts. The 7-falsifier pre-statement
(F_α ... F_η) is exemplary discipline; 3 hold, 3 fail informatively,
1 N/A — the failures themselves carry new structural content (Phase-
Lim regime split + J*=1 trough mechanism).

**Failure-mode classification:** N/A — refinement, not a fresh attack.

**Complexity / numerical correctness:** Verified. The Gaussian-Y
closed form `rel(m) = m · Σ_j [Φ((j+1−α)/σ_n) − Φ((j−α)/σ_n)]` and
the wrapped-Gaussian-density limit (Poisson-summation / Jacobi-ϑ
form) are standard. The peak-height calculation at m=110 (predicted
21.5 vs empirical 22.4) is internally consistent. The σ_Y ≥ 2 regime
boundary for the Taylor-collapse-to-WG approximation is mathematically
sound.

**Novelty defensibility:** B at lower edge. The five new structural
facts each refine E1.3 inline. The J*=1 bounded-support trough
mechanism at α ∉ {0, 0.5} is the strongest contribution — a
structural anomaly identified, mechanism explained (bounded e support
truncates Gaussian-Y's right-tail mass), and quantified (worst-case
17× over-count at m=200, vs S218's J*=2 worst-case 5× at m=29).
Self-grade defense paragraph correctly notes: "Not A-grade because
(i) does not produce a polylog opening for any π-related computation;
(ii) the Empirical-r identity from S218 remains the gold-standard
predictor — none of the new closed-form candidates outperform it".
That is the right A-grade rejection for this work.

**Edge citation accuracy:** Verified. E1.3 (target), S146 (LSB-side
bit-RH-shadow), S199 (cross-modulus universality), S218 (Empirical-r
exact + Gaussian-Y closed form). The lineage F1 → F1.a → F1.a.i →
F1.a.i.γ is correctly traced.

**Three successor challenges proposed (γ.i, γ.ii, γ.iii)** — meets
the self-extension requirement of CLAUDE.md "Autonomy invariants".

**Verdict:** B confirmed. No demotion.

---

### S239 — Parity-stripped trinity (PARADIGM-SHIFT)

**Files audited:**
* `experiments/constructions/parity_stripped_trinity/definition.md`
* `experiments/constructions/parity_stripped_trinity/parity_stripped_trinity.py`
* `experiments/constructions/parity_stripped_trinity/parity_stripped_trinity_results.md`
* `experiments/constructions/parity_stripped_trinity/sequential_strip_check.py`
* `experiments/constructions/parity_stripped_trinity/sequential_bdj_check.py`
* `experiments/constructions/parity_stripped_trinity/*.json`

**Tested-before check:** No prior paradigm-shift session has measured
all three statistics (E2.20 Mahler / E2.21 Newman L^∞ / E2.31 BDJ
m_4) jointly under the same parity-strip transformation. S204 noted
the BDJ m_4 violation "carried by a single isolated eigenvalue ≈ 89%
parity rank-1". S134 left the Mahler deficit's mechanism as "TBD; HL
singular series most plausible". S168 / S190 supplied the squarefree-q
spike formula. S239 composes these via a single sequential-strip
operator and produces the inversion observation (22% vs 83%) — that
is genuine new project content.

**Failure-mode classification:** N/A — refinement-shape session in
paradigm-shift mode, not a fresh attack.

**Mode discipline:** Verified. No `WebFetch` / `WebSearch`. The
construction (orthogonal projection along (−1)^n + sequential
additive-Fourier projection on V_q^prim) is elementary linear
algebra, already USED in the project. No new cross-domain technique.
No new ATTACK_VECTORS entries. Mode constraints honored.

**Pre-stated falsifiers F1-F4:** F1 PASS (numerical floor < 10⁻⁷);
F2 PARTIAL (DC peak supersedes naive prediction; non-trivial peak at
q=3 with HL-predicted magnitude); F3 → F3.b sharpened ("residual-
sourced" → "sequentially major-arc-sourced, broadly distributed");
F4 → F4.b sharpened (83% closure at Q=2; residual ~17% from q ≥ 3
with explicit constant 0.15). The sharpening of pre-stated falsifiers
is itself a B-grade contribution (CLAUDE.md "B-grade Refinement of
an existing edge with a precise new statement that extends its scope").

**Novelty defensibility:** B confirmed. The hierarchy decomposition
table

|             | q=2  | q ≤ 7 | q ≤ 29 |
| Newman L^∞  | 100% | 100%  | 100%   |
| BDJ m_4     |  83% |  93%  |  95%   |
| Mahler def. |  22% |  57%  |  84%   |

is a NEW project artefact. The 22%/83% inversion between E2.20 and
E2.31 is empirical and was not previously stated. The structural
explanation (Mahler is a log-flat geometric mean while m_4 is an L^4
power-sum, hence different per-q weights) is correct intuition though
not derived rigorously — left as "Open question 1" in the results
file. The session honestly notes "the exact 22% vs 83% inversion is
empirically verified, not derived; the predicted asymptotic at large
Q would require analytical continuation of the Jensen-integral
expansion in HL major arcs (open question)".

**Self-grade defense:** Correctly notes "Not A-grade because: (i) no
new theorem; (ii) no new identity; (iii) no algorithmic content. The
construction is elementary; novelty is in the EXPERIMENT, not the
technique." That is the right A-grade rejection.

**Edge citation accuracy:** Verified. E2.20 (refined), E2.21 (used as
subtractand), E2.31 (refined), E1.6 + E2.10 (parity bisection
identity), S168 / S190 (squarefree-q spike formula). All citations
accurate.

**Verdict:** B confirmed. No demotion.

---

## Highest-value next-action

**Thread 7 (P3 polylog approximation) is queued in `.commit_state`
with a full 5-slot plan.** Slot 1: build partial-sum evaluator
`π(x) ≈ R(x) − Σ_{ρ: |γ| ≤ T} 2 Re(li(x^ρ))` for K ∈ {1, log x,
log² x, log³ x, x^{1/4}, x^{1/2}} zeros, measure empirical
ε(x, K) at x ∈ {10⁶, 10⁸, 10¹⁰, 10¹²}, fit ε vs K.

**Why this is the right pick under the A-grade scarcity warning:**
P3 is the highest-EV partial-positive target on `OPEN_POSITIVE_TARGETS.md`
(per .commit_state thread_7_a_grade_targets). A success at slot 1
with empirical ε(x, log² x) ≈ √x · log log x / log⁴ x would be a
strictly better-than-√x polylog bound — the first sub-√x polylog
approximation, A-grade per CLAUDE.md (b) "a working algorithm beating
an existing benchmark". Even partial success delivers a quantitative
ε vs K characterisation across x decades that no prior session has
produced. **The framework needs A-grade-shaped attempts. Thread 7 is
the next one queued. The next commit slot must pick it up.**

**No new ATTACK_VECTORS entry written this critique.** Section §H
(cross-x amortisation) covers the related machinery; OPEN_POSITIVE_TARGETS.md
§P3 covers Thread 7. The commit-state recommended_next_action already
codifies the slot 1 plan.

**Inline reinforcement noted in RESEARCH_AGENDA.md** below: Thread 7
is now ACTIVE per .commit_state; the critique reinforces it as the
single highest-EV next move.

---

## Cross-domain technique registry status

No new techniques imported by S237 / S238 / S239. S237 is re-verify
mode; S238 is direct extension of S218 closed-form analysis; S239
is paradigm-shift mode with the explicit "no cross-domain import"
constraint. No registry updates needed.

---

## Summary

Three sessions audited, zero inflated grades, zero demotions, zero
new CLOSED_PATHS rows, zero new EDGES entries (all refinements
inline as required). The three-session slice is honest steady-state
work. **The 30-session A-grade drought (zero A across S210-S239)
crosses the 20-session warning threshold by 50% and is the dominant
finding of this critique.** The next commit slot must execute Thread 7
slot 1; the framework cannot continue producing all-B/all-C output
indefinitely without action on the warning.

## How to use this file

**Starting a session:**
1. Read this file to find an arc to continue.
2. If no arc fits, check NOVELTY_CHALLENGES.md for a single-session target.
3. If you start an arc that wasn't here, add it.

**During a session:**
1. Mark your arc as `Status: IN PROGRESS — <session number>`.
2. Don't context-switch between arcs unless one is blocked.

**Ending a session:**
1. Update the arc's milestones (check off completed items).
2. Update the arc's `Next action:` to whatever the next agent should do.
3. If you completed the arc, move it to "Closed arcs" with a one-line
   summary and pointer to the resulting artifact.
4. If your session created a new arc (e.g., a research direction that
   needs follow-up), add it to "Active arcs" with status NOT STARTED.

**The next-action discipline matters most.** Agents have short context
windows. A clear next-action lets the next agent pick up without
re-reading the whole arc history.
